label: model_selection_iter1
prompt:
You are the Model Selection judge. The plan below has already been decided; your one
job is to commit to a concrete model identifier and its hyperparameters.

## Plan

{
  "strategy": "Attempt 1: replace the linear baseline with a gradient-boosted tree ensemble, which is the family that actually raises the ranking on spambase's sparse, highly skewed word-frequency counts. Fit hist_gbdt on all 2,760 training rows (no internal early-stopping slice), with enough capacity to capture the interactions logreg cannot express: learning_rate 0.06, max_iter 500, max_leaf_nodes 31, min_samples_leaf 10, l2_regularization 1.0. Keep preprocessing minimal — median impute (no missing values exist anyway), no scaling, since trees are scale-invariant and the goal here is ranking quality, not the operating point. Leave class_weight at default: the 1.54 imbalance is mild and the default cut on a well-ranked GBDT ranking is already near-optimal; I will read cut_headroom, recall vs specificity, roc_auc and balanced_accuracy_at_best_cut from this attempt to decide whether attempts 2-5 should push capacity<path> further (ranking axis) or nudge class_weight (operating-point axis).",
  "model_family": "gbdt",
  "candidate_models": [
    "hist_gbdt",
    "xgboost",
    "random_forest"
  ],
  "hyperparams": {
    "max_iter": 500,
    "learning_rate": 0.06,
    "max_leaf_nodes": 31,
    "min_samples_leaf": 10,
    "l2_regularization": 1.0,
    "early_stopping": false
  },
  "preprocessing": {
    "impute": "median",
    "scale": false,
    "missing_indicator": false,
    "missing_count": false
  },
  "changes_from_last": "No prior attempt. Relative to the card's baseline: family changes from linear (logreg + standard scaling) to a boosted tree ensemble (hist_gbdt), scaling is dropped as unnecessary for trees, and capacity is set explicitly (500 boosting iterations at lr 0.06, 31 leaves, l2 1.0) with early_stopping disabled so all 2,760 training rows are used.",
  "rationale": "The goal bar (0.967 balanced_accuracy) sits above the baseline's ranking ceiling (balanced_accuracy_at_best_cut 0.9233, KS 0.8466), so no threshold or class-weight move on the logreg ranking can reach it — the required KS is 0.934, i.e. the ranking itself must improve by ~0.087. That means a family change, and gradient-boosted trees are the family with the best-documented ranking gain on spambase-style data: 57 highly skewed, mostly zero-inflated frequency counts whose signal lives in thresholds (\"more than 0.1% '$' AND many capitals\") and in interactions between spam markers and ham markers (hp, george, edu, 650) — exactly the axis-aligned threshold structure a linear model in raw units cannot represent, and the reason its recall stalls at 0.856. hist_gbdt is cheap (cost 3, 2,760 rows × 57 columns fits far inside 2GB / 600s), handles skew and outliers without transformation, and needs no scaling. Capacity is set high but regularised: many small-shrinkage trees (lr 0.06 × 500 iters) with min_samples_leaf 10 and l2 1.0 to control the variance that 2,760 rows invites; early_stopping is left off because the default 10% slice would cost 276 of those rows and make the score non-comparable to attempts that keep them. Class balance is 1.54:1 — mild — so the default cut should sit near the optimum; I deliberately spend attempt 1 entirely on the ranking axis and use the returned cut_headroom, specificity<path> and balanced_accuracy_at_best_cut to attribute any remaining shortfall before touching the operating point.",
  "unsupported_claims": [],
  "source": "llm",
  "iteration": 1
}
